questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "She was in the pink of health after the surgery." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: In the pink of health means in perfect health.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The two neighbours have been at loggerheads for years over the boundary wall." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: At loggerheads means quarrelling or in sharp dispute.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Raman was on cloud nine when he got the job offer." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: On cloud nine means very happy.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Priya got cold feet just before the interview." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Cold feet means sudden fear or loss of nerve.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "After his illness, he decided to turn over a new leaf." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: begin a new and better way of life
questions.explanation: It means to make a fresh start.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Winning the state-level award was a feather in her cap." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: an achievement to be proud of
questions.explanation: A feather in one's cap is an honour or achievement.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The teacher went the extra mile to help weak students." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: To go the extra mile is to do more than is required.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "With a small salary, he finds it difficult to make ends meet." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: earn just enough to pay for basic needs
questions.explanation: Make ends meet means to manage on the money one has.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The donation was a drop in the ocean compared with what was needed." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: A drop in the ocean is a tiny amount compared with the need.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The brothers finally buried the hatchet after twenty years." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: To bury the hatchet is to make peace.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The fireman reached the spot in the nick of time." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: In the nick of time means barely in time.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "A promotion for Meena is on the cards this year." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: On the cards means probable.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The company's profits have grown by leaps and bounds." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: By leaps and bounds means with rapid progress.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Do not take his harsh words to heart." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Taking something to heart means being greatly affected by it.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The minister only paid lip service to the cause of education." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Lip service is insincere verbal support.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The clerk has an axe to grind in this dispute." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: An axe to grind means a private interest influencing one's actions.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "We went on a wild goose chase looking for the address." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: A wild goose chase is a futile pursuit.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Do not jump the gun and announce the results before they are declared." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: To jump the gun is to act prematurely.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Since the quarrel, Kavitha has been giving me the cold shoulder." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Cold shoulder means unfriendly treatment.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "He landed in hot water for submitting false bills." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: In hot water means in trouble.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "As a young actor, he rubbed shoulders with famous stars." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: To rub shoulders is to meet and mix with people.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "He pulled strings to get his son admitted to the college." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Pulling strings means using influential contacts.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "Do not pass the buck; take responsibility for the error." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: shift the blame onto someone else
questions.explanation: To pass the buck is to transfer responsibility to another.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "He got the sack for being constantly absent." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Get the sack means to be fired.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The office files were at sixes and sevens after the shifting." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: At sixes and sevens means in confusion.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "She made the remark tongue in cheek, so nobody took it seriously." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Tongue in cheek means said ironically, not seriously.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The doctors kept the infection at bay with strong antibiotics." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Keeping something at bay means preventing it from coming near or harming.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The new manager expects every employee to toe the line." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: To toe the line is to obey rules and conform.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The matter was a hot potato, so the officers avoided it." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: a controversial issue difficult to handle
questions.explanation: A hot potato is an awkward subject that people avoid handling.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "His argument does not hold water." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: An argument that does not hold water is unsound.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "The news came out of the blue and shocked everybody." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
questions.explanation: Out of the blue means suddenly and without warning.

questions.questionText: Read the sentence: "In a fit of anger he took the law into his own hands." Which option gives the meaning of the idiomatic expression used in it?
options: acted on his own without legal authority
questions.explanation: Taking the law into one's hands means punishing or acting without legal right.
